I do believe models and quants can explain some part of the likely outcome of the price of an asset, but, expectations and psychology have an important impact on the final result. The chances of a company to deliver sometimes are less important than the sentiment of the investors. You can throw a monte Carlo simulation and use quantitative methods to maximize your sharpie ratio, but then, enter the human factors, and  these may drive / drag all variables related to spending, debt, conflict resolution, etc., and so, the model becomes very sensible in a day-to-day basis. Game theory is an interesting field.
